name: File Manager
description: Browse, view and edit the open project in the right work panel: a full directory tree with per-file-type icons, a left file list that can be collapsed as a whole, syntax-highlighted editing, a Markdown preview, PDF previews, image and media viewing, CSV/JSON structured views, read-only SQLite browsing with a SQL query box, a context menu for creating and renaming, filename search, switching between the folders of a multi-folder project (the folder name in the header opens the list of folders and the choice is remembered per project), and host-driven open requests for a single file (including session scratch and attachment paths outside the project). Files and folders can also be deleted from the context menu (directories are removed as a whole, with a confirmation prompt first). It also tracks git: the file list marks which files are modified and which are new (folders carry a rollup of the whole subtree), shows the changed line counts (+N/−N), and the right pane can show a file's actual changes against the last commit (line by line; untracked files read as all-new, staged and unstaged edits labelled separately). With no git, or outside a repository, the marks disappear and everything else behaves as before. It also watches the project: changes made outside this view (another editor, a git checkout, a build step, a second window) are picked up and re-read automatically instead of requiring the refresh button — both refresh buttons are unchanged, and a toolbar switch turns auto-refresh off. For a file with changes the toolbar is one mutually exclusive tab group — Edit / Preview / Changes — so Changes is reachable from either side and the two views can never occupy the content area at the same time.The context menu also offers "Copy relative path" and "Copy absolute path", plus an "Open with…" submenu that expands on hover and lists the editors actually installed on this machine (the system default app, plus VS Code, Zed, Chrome, Edge, Zen and the like — only those really present), filtered by file type so a browser is offered only for the web files it can actually render (never for a .tsx), so a file or folder can be handed straight to one of them. That probe runs once at startup and is cached per day on disk, shared between windows; it locates editors through the App Paths / StartMenuInternet registry keys, PATH and a few fixed install locations, and never walks directories. Files and folders can also be deleted from the context menu (directories are removed as a whole, with a confirmation prompt first). It also tracks git: the file list marks which files are modified and which are new (folders carry a rollup of the whole subtree), shows the changed line counts (+N/−N), and the right pane can show a file's actual changes against the last commit (line by line; untracked files read as all-new, staged and unstaged edits labelled separately). With no git, or outside a repository, the marks disappear and everything else behaves as before. It also watches the project: changes made outside this view (another editor, a git checkout, a build step, a second window) are picked up and re-read automatically instead of requiring the refresh button — both refresh buttons are unchanged, and a toolbar switch turns auto-refresh off. For a file with changes the toolbar is one mutually exclusive tab group — Edit / Preview / Changes — so Changes is reachable from either side and the two views can never occupy the content area at the same time. The context menu can open HTML, HTM, and XHTML files in the host's built-in browser.

en.safetyNotes: Databases are opened strictly read-only (readOnly + PRAGMA query_only) and the query box only accepts single read-only statements, so a database can be browsed but never modified. fs.read is declared only for the three host-mediated actions "open with default app", "open HTML in the built-in browser", and "show in folder" (same permission and scope as the bundled Files view); the plugin's own reading and writing goes through Node's fs inside the plugin's own process — the host permission gateway does not mediate these calls, and the manifest cannot declare a whole-tree write. Deletion goes through the same path: it is performed by the plugin's own Node fs, is bound by the same root containment checks and credential deny list, explicitly refuses to delete the project root itself, and is recorded in the write audit log. Root-relative paths are confined by the plugin itself to the selected registered folder root of the project: resolved paths must stay inside that root (symlink and junction escapes are refused), and credential paths (.env*, .ssh/, *.pem, .git/**) are refused. When a project is registered as several local folders, the containment base is still exactly one of those roots at a time — never their union — and an absolute path the host asks this view to open that lies under another root of the same project is accepted by first switching the base to the containing root and then resolving that path relative to it, with the same containment checks applied. One exception is deliberate and is NOT covered by that containment guarantee: when the host asks this view to open a file it picked itself outside the project (a session scratch or attachment path), the request is an absolute OS path and the plugin reads and writes it with raw Node fs, with no root containment; the credential deny list is still enforced for those paths (checked against the raw, the normalised and the realpath form), and they are still written atomically and audited. Saves are atomic (temp file + rename), and overwriting a file changed outside the editor asks first. Images and media are read up to their own size limits (8 MiB / 24 MiB) and handed to the view as base64 data URIs; binaries such as zip or exe are never decoded, only reported as unsupported. No network access; the plugin data directory only holds settings and a write audit log.Git integration only runs git's read-only subcommands (status / diff / rev-parse) from the user's own working copy: no index writes, no network, nothing inside .git/**. Status runs with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 / GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 / GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1; every subcommand has a 5s timeout and an output cap, and if git is not on PATH the plugin probes the usual install locations once. When git still isn't available the only consequence is "no status" — listing, reading, writing, saving and deleting are untouched. Paths handed to git are root-relative and pass the root containment check and the credential deny list first; git is merely asked how those files are doing. Diffs come from git diff for tracked files; an untracked new file is read by the plugin and shown with every line added (256 KiB cap), and oversized or binary files say so instead of being silently truncated. Badges and counts come from one snapshot cached for 2s, and the plugin's own saves invalidate it immediately. File watching (0.8.0) uses Node's own fs.watch on the **currently selected folder root**, recursive and non-persistent (it never holds the plugin process awake when nothing changes). Changes are only read, never written, no network, nothing inside .git/** — events under .git/ and node_modules/ are dropped outright and credential paths are still never reported (watching is not a back door around the deny list). The plugin's own writes (temp file + rename) are noted first, so a same-path event within 1.5s does not count as an external change; without that, every Ctrl+S would re-load the user's own document. Events are debounced for 250ms into a bounded cursor history (400 entries) which the view collects every 1.2s (the host gives plugins no push channel to a view), and the round is skipped while the panel is hidden. **An open file with no unsaved changes is re-read automatically; with unsaved changes the view only warns and never overwrites** — silently discarding what someone just typed is the worst kind of automation. Switching the base switches the watcher, and unloading the plugin closes it. If the runtime cannot watch recursively, auto-refresh is simply off while manual refresh and everything else behave exactly as before. "Open with…" is performed by this plugin's own main process, which spawns the chosen editor using Node capabilities that process already had and no extra permission: the executable can only come from the list the plugin detected itself (the view passes an id, never a path), the target passes the same root containment check and credential deny list as every other channel, the spawn goes through no shell with a single absolute path as its argument (so there is no command-line injection surface), and the child is detached with stdio ignored so the editor outlives the panel without holding the plugin process open. Every launch is recorded in the write audit log. Detection only reads the registry and PATH, writes nothing outside the plugin data directory, and caches its result per day (editors.json); if the probe is unavailable the only consequence is one menu layer fewer. SSH workspaces use the scoped Host SDK for read-only directory and text/image previews; remote paths never reach local Node fs. Requires remote workspace metadata and workspacePluginFiles capability; search, Git, watch and editing remain unavailable remotely.

author: Tioit-Wang
changelog: Desktop hotfix: directory locations from the host open in the tree instead of failing as file reads. Desktop hotfix: scoped remote reads and theme-aware editor search. Release 0.9.0: the context menu adds "Copy relative path", "Copy absolute path" and an "Open with…" submenu that expands on hover and lists the programs actually installed on this machine (the system default app plus VS Code, Zed, Chrome, Edge, Zen and the like), filtered by file type (browsers appear only for web files they can render, never Chrome for a .tsx); picking one opens the current entry in it. Editor detection never walks directories: it only reads the registry App Paths (HKLM / WOW6432Node / HKCU) and StartMenuInternet shell\open\command keys, looks up candidate command names on PATH and stats a few fixed install locations once each; every source is O(candidates), the four registry queries run in parallel, about 600ms cold. Results are cached per date in editors.json in the plugin data directory, probed once a day and shared across instances (a second window or launch reads the cache). Executables never leave the main process: the view only gets an id and display name and can only pass back an id; the opened path passes the same root containment check and credential deny list as every other channel; spawn uses no shell and a single absolute path argument; the child is detached + stdio ignore + unref; every launch is recorded in the write audit. On Windows only real .exe files are accepted (.cmd/.bat shims need cmd.exe, an unnecessary injection surface). Without any editor the submenu keeps only "System default app", never an entry that does nothing. The submenu supports hover and →/←/↑↓/Home/End/Escape and flips to the left of its trigger when it would overflow the viewport. New offline check pnpm verify:editors. Release 0.8.2: fix own saves (Ctrl+S) still being treated as external changes. 0.8.0 only noted "I wrote this file myself", but the recursive watcher on Windows also reports change <dir> once for every ancestor directory of a written file (tested: writing src/deep/x.ts reports change src/deep and change src), and those events were not suppressed, so any Ctrl+S could reload the just-saved document (losing cursor and scroll position, exactly what 0.8.0 meant to prevent). noteSelfWrite now records every ancestor directory along with the file path (the root itself emits no such event); pnpm verify:watch adds this regression (unit + nested-path end to end), failing reliably before the fix and passing 6 runs in a row after it. Also fixes a timing race in verify:watch where late directory events from the previous step (external create / delete) landed in the current save window and occasionally failed (1 in 5 runs); it now waits until two consecutive rounds show no change before taking the cursor. On non-Windows platforms the change is a no-op; behaviour is identical to 0.8.1. Release 0.8.1: fix preview and diff overlapping when opening changes in preview mode. Two structural causes: (1) "Changes" was a separate toggle outside the tablist (aria-pressed), not exclusive with "Edit / Preview", so "preview + changes" was a valid combination; (2) the content area rendered each view by its own boolean, so the Markdown preview and the diff, both full height, mounted together and overlapped. Both are fixed: the decision is centralised in the single-valued contentKind() of views-src/src/lib/pane.ts (one view at a time, changes over preview) and tabs()/activeTabKey() ("Edit / Preview / Changes" in one exclusive group with a unique selection); EditorPane renders only that value, and "Changes" is the third tab, so switching to edit or preview closes it. The Changes tab is offered only for text files (images / media / databases own the content area), and tabs() de-duplicates modes (duplicate keys break React reuse). The regression is pinned in verify-viewers.mjs: an exhaustive input scan asserts a single content view, all ten views reachable, "changes beat preview / preview returns after closing changes" and a unique selected tab. Release 0.8.0: file watching: files changed outside the editor (another editor, git checkout, build output, another window) are re-read automatically and the list refreshes within 1.2 seconds, no need to press "Refresh". The main process opens one recursive fs.watch on the current base root (persistent: false; events under .git/ and node_modules/ are dropped, credential paths are never reported), debounces changes for 250ms into a bounded cursor history, and the view polls the delta (the host has no plugin-to-view push channel). Three explicit rules: an open file without unsaved changes is re-read automatically; with unsaved changes only a notice bar appears and nothing is overwritten; the plugin's own saves are noted first, and a same-path event within 1.5 seconds is not an external change (otherwise every Ctrl+S would reload your own document). Changed parent folders are relisted, with mtime, size, git badges, created and deleted entries. A new "Auto-refresh" switch at the top (can be turned off; disabled with an explanation when the runtime cannot watch), both manual refresh buttons unchanged. New offline check pnpm verify:watch next to pnpm verify:git (noise filtering + own-write suppression + real fs.watch end to end + the view's pure decision functions). Release 0.7.0: git integration: the file list marks which files are modified and which are new with a badge letter and colour (green A added / amber M modified / red D deleted / blue R renamed / purple U conflicted), file rows end with +N/−N, folders show a rollup of their whole subtree (number of affected files), and hover gives the full description (staged / untracked). The top of the left list summarises the current branch and the file count per change kind. A new "Changes" view on the right: when the open file has changes the toolbar shows a "Changes" button (also "View changes" in the context menu) that opens a line-by-line unified diff, +/− coloured, line numbers on both sides, hunk headers keep the enclosing function name, staged and unstaged sections labelled; untracked new files show as all-added, and deleted files still show their removed lines. Status and diffs come from the real git in the working copy (read-only subcommands status / diff / rev-parse, 5s timeout, output cap, 2s result cache); the plugin's own saves invalidate the cache immediately; the plugin parses the porcelain / numstat / unified diff forms itself (pinned by verify-git.mjs). Without git, outside a repository, or on timeout everything degrades to "no status", and listing, reading, writing and saving are unchanged; new offline check pnpm verify:git (pure function fixtures + end to end with a real temporary repository). Release 0.6.1: fix the Markdown preview being too narrow and not following the sidebar divider: a leftover max-width:78ch on .md-body pinned the preview body to a fixed column of about 78 characters that did not move when dragging the split divider; it is now max-width:100%, so the preview fills the editor area and follows the split width live (tested in a headless browser). Release 0.6.0: deletion: "Delete" in the context menu now really deletes; folders are removed recursively as a whole after a confirmation dialog; path limits match writes exactly: inside the selected folder root, refusing the root itself, credential paths and node_modules, recorded in the write audit. The view also changed: the sidebar toggle moves to the far left, the toolbar drops the new file / new folder / rename / move to buttons (these actions live in the context menu), the file address is now absolute and copied on click, and image previews support wheel zoom and dragging. Release 0.5.2: fix the list not following a folder switch. The host reports directories with forward slashes (C:/Users/…), while the plugin stored its memory via path.resolve with backslashes (C:\Users\…), and the comparison only tried "as is" and "case-insensitive", so the memory matched no root and the containment base fell back to the primary folder: the header name changed (the view still matched with its own raw string), but list and editor stayed on the primary folder, and the choice was not remembered. Path comparison is now separator-independent, and already corrupted memory entries are recovered. Release 0.5.1: fix "Open with default app" and "Show in folder" possibly opening the wrong file after switching folders in a project group. Both channels are executed by the host and only accept workspace-relative paths, so with the base switched to a sibling folder the host resolved them against the primary folder and opened the other file when both folders had the same name; with a non-primary base an absolute path is now sent (the host has a matching narrow allowance for absolute paths under the project's registered folder roots, see ADR 0253). With the primary base the behaviour is identical to 0.5.0 / 0.4. Release 0.5.0: the host can register one project as several local folders (workspace.get and the initial handshake roots / projectId). The folder name at the top left of the panel becomes a switcher: with more than one folder it opens the group's folder menu (primary folder marked, current one checked), keyboard accessible with aria-haspopup / aria-expanded, closed by Escape or a click outside; with a single folder (or an older host without group info) the header is identical to 0.4.0, with no dead entry. Switching resets tree, expansion, selection, search and open files, and still asks for confirmation on unsaved changes first; cancelling changes nothing. The browsed folder is remembered per project (key p:<projectId>; r:<primary root path> when the host gives no projectId; a value is trusted only if it matches a current root, otherwise the primary root is used; at most 20 entries, evicted by most recent write); new projects start at the primary folder. The containment base is always exactly one root, never widened to the union of the group: tree / read / write / create / rename / move / search / SQLite all resolve against the selected root, and .., symlink and junction escapes and the credential deny list are not relaxed. Host open requests take three forms: project-relative paths use the primary root (switching back to it first if another root is shown); an absolute path under another root of the same project switches to the containing root and opens relative to it (ancestors expanded, row highlighted); absolute paths outside the group keep the 0.4.0 external behaviour (not in the tree, no highlight, base unchanged). Release 0.4.0: host-driven open requests: the host can ask the view to open a file; both the ?piViewOpen= payload of the view entry URL (read once synchronously at mount, so it cannot race the page) and the view:open push (live updates after load; before load completes the host rewrites the URL and reloads) are handled, and a duplicate delivery is processed once; project paths still expand and load their ancestors, and the dirty buffer guard still applies (unsaved edits are never discarded silently). Absolute paths outside the project chosen by the host (session scratch directory / attachments) can be opened and saved too: the view sets an external flag and the plugin skips root containment for them (they are outside the root by definition), while the credential deny list stays fully enforced (checked on the raw, normalised and realpath forms), and saves are still atomic and audited. The left file list can be collapsed as a whole: it collapses automatically (and persists) on host open requests, keeps the split width and restores it on expanding; the toolbar gains a keyboard-accessible toggle. Release 0.3.1: adds "Open with default app" and "Show in folder" (via the host's fs.openDefault / fs.reveal, which is why fs.read is declared, with the same permission and scope as the built-in Files view; folders are invalid for these actions, so they are offered for files only). Release 0.3.0: from "edit text only" to "see all kinds of files": image viewing (png/jpg/gif/webp/avif/bmp/ico/svg, fit to window and actual size, checkerboard, pixel size and file size), audio and video playback (mp4/mov/webm/mkv and mp3/wav/flac/ogg and more, no autoplay, a clear message for unsupported codecs), CSV/TSV tables (1000 rows per page by default, adjustable and remembered, click headers to sort ascending / descending / off, sticky row numbers and header, right-aligned numbers, full value on hover), a JSON tree, and read-only SQLite browsing with an SQL query box (read-only in three layers: readOnly + PRAGMA query_only + a single read-only statement allowlist; bytes never reach the view, so databases of hundreds of MB open). Binary files (zip/apk/exe and similar) clearly say preview is not supported. Also fixes a severe save defect: after a successful save the editor document was reloaded with the old content from when it was opened (now loadToken distinguishes "loaded from disk" from "mtime updated after save"), plus "writes without changes", "pressing Ctrl+S twice conflicts with itself", "the user had switched files when a save returned" and "Ctrl+S does nothing without editor focus". Release 0.2.0: fixes missing syntax highlighting (dropping basicSetup's built-in fallback highlighter), language resolution via an explicit registry, and adds a context menu and a Markdown preview / edit toggle. Release 0.1.0: first release, with a full directory tree in the right work panel + syntax-highlighted editing and saving + create / rename / move + filename search. Unreleased: adds an offline read-only PDF preview with continuous scrolling, single / double / separate-cover layouts, full-text search, and a sidebar with thumbnails, a nested outline and document info; fit width keeps stable page proportions and handles mixed sizes, lazy loading and panel / sidebar resizing. Improves error recovery for later pages and fixes automatic re-reading of files; per-file limit 24 MiB; see CHANGELOG.md for details.
